lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Correction assessment: exact roots, evaluation, and irrationality

sections.title: ma-g8-mathematics-c01-assessment — 30 points, 6 prompts
sections.directions: Work every prompt independently. No instructional support is given during this assessment. A squaring and cubing reference table is permitted.

items.prompt: Write the exact solution or solutions of each equation using root notation: x² = 49, x² = 11, x³ = 27, x³ = 5. For each, state how many real solutions the equation has and why. (6 points)
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Evaluate exactly, without a calculator: √121, √(16/49), ∛64, ∛(1/27). Verify two of your four answers using the inverse operation and show that verification. (6 points)
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: For √45 and ∛50, state the two consecutive whole numbers each value lies between and explain how you know without a calculator. Then explain why neither can be written as an exact whole number. (5 points)
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Explain why √2 is irrational but √49 is rational. Give a reason rather than an assertion; reference the decimal expansion, the ratio-of-integers definition, or the informal contradiction argument. (5 points)
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A learner writes: “x² = 25, so x = 5,” and “∛(−27) has no real solution because you cannot take a root of a negative.” Identify what is wrong with each statement, correct it, and explain why the error is tempting. (4 points)
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A square garden bed must enclose 20 square feet. Give the exact side length in root notation, classify it as rational or irrational with a reason, give an approximation appropriate for buying lumber, and explain why the exact and rounded forms are each correct for their own purpose. (4 points)
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
